english.title: Drive / attempt to drive vehicle and fail to allow blood specimen taken while incapable of giving consent to be analysed
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been informed that a specimen of blood had been taken from you under section 7A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 at a time when you were incapable of consenting to its taking, failed, without reasonable excuse, to give your permission for a laboratory test of that specimen
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7A(6) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 7A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 was inserted by section 56 of the Police Reform Act 2002
(ii) This offence should only be used where the test (which was not consented to) would be for ascertaining the donors ability to drive or the proportion of alcohol at the time offender was driving or attempting to drive. In other circumstances (e.g. where suspected that the donor was 'in charge' of vehicle) H10942 should be used.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Obligatory disqualification. (Licence endorsed three to eleven points).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
